Core: Driver or manager completes a primary task safely.
Selection: User chooses one or many valid operational values.
Inputs: User enters operational data with validation and recovery.
Mobile: Driver acts inside constrained touch-first screens.
Maps: Driver finds stations, compares details, and starts route handoff.
Navigation: User moves through hierarchy, steps, pages, and sections.
Dashboards: Fleet manager scans, filters, drills in, and exports evidence.
Configuration: Admin changes users, roles, vehicles, or permissions with audit.
Feedback: System reports status, recovery, progress, or absence.
Overlay: User gets contextual choices without losing origin or focus.
Layout: Content is grouped, revealed, or resized with Frame rules.
Display: Product data is scanned, compared, labeled, or grouped.
Data: User sorts, compares, toggles, and explains data.
Motion: State change communicates cause without becoming decorative.

fallbackProfile: User completes a real product job.

scenarioCopy.Selection: Fleet manager scopes a dashboard filter and expects option state, stale data, and permissions to be explicit.
scenarioCopy.Inputs: Admin enters operational data and needs validation, helper text, save behavior, and recovery.
scenarioCopy.Feedback: System reports progress, error, or absence while preserving the user's next action.
scenarioCopy.Overlay: User opens contextual actions and must be able to escape, select, or recover focus.
scenarioCopy.Dashboards: Fleet manager scans a metric, understands threshold, and drills into evidence.
scenarioCopy.Mobile: Driver acts quickly on a constrained screen with touch-safe controls and clear failure states.
scenarioCopy.fallback: The component appears inside a real fleet or driver process with state, recovery, and accessibility requirements.

familyStandards.standardCopy: This page uses the group standard for {{family}}. It is not yet a hand-authored gold page like Button, but it now includes real scenario, demos, states, responsive behavior, API, tests, and quality gates.
mustProve: Responsive behavior is explicit for mobile, tablet, laptop, and desktop.
familyStandards.demoCopy: The demo is generated from the {{group}} standard, so every component in this family gets a real state surface instead of a placeholder card.
familyStandards.stateMatrixCopy: Document the states users must recognize and the recovery path for blocked or failed states.
responsiveBehavior: {{title}} must define mobile, tablet, laptop, and desktop behavior.
Compact view cannot hide required labels or recovery actions.
Overflow moves into Menu, Bottom Sheet, Dialog, or Pagination depending on group.
Touch, keyboard, and screen reader behavior must remain equivalent.
apiRows: Required for input, selection, data, and navigation components.
State changes copy, ARIA, and visual treatment.
Maps to Frame spacing and Voice scale.
Emits semantic payload, not DOM implementation detail.
Accessible name is never optional for interactive controls.
testRows: {{title}} renders the correct role, accessible name, visible label, and required state attributes.
{{title}} exposes required props as observable DOM state, not private implementation detail.
{{title}} covers {{states}} with visible, assistive, and recoverable behavior.
Pointer, keyboard, touch, escape, focus restoration, and duplicate-action blocking match the component family pattern.
Reduced motion, high contrast, screen reader naming, focus visibility, target size, and long localized text do not break layout.
Mobile, tablet, laptop, and desktop behavior is explicit; compact density cannot hide labels or recovery actions.
No raw color, spacing, typography, radius, elevation, icon, or motion values outside foundation-backed component tokens.
familyStandards.testingModelCopy: The testing model is shared by every component. {{title}} is the applied example, not a one-off exception.
